angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 438,291 km at 12.78 pc = 0.46 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 78.2268 +/- 0.0182 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 12.78 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.63 +/- 0.027 solar radii from Kunimoto et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 101581 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...47K/abstract): 438,291 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.653 +/- 0.028 solar masses from Kunimoto et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 101581 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...47K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4675 +/- 53 K from Kunimoto et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 101581 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...47K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kunimoto et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 101581 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...47K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hip-56998.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.654, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
